requirement:
Each language's fingerprint rules determine which attachments
contribute to the owning item's structural hash.
rationale:
The requirement says each language's fingerprint rules decide which attachments contribute to the owning item's structural hash. I took the per-language rules from the `fingerprints` requirements in `md/requirements/sdk/sources/*.md` and checked that the tests exercise each rule through a hash comparison.

**Rust.** Doc comments and attributes contribute. Plain comments don't.
- `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` covers all three.
- Changing the plain comment text (`{cite}` `a.b` to `c.d`) and reflowing the body leave the hash and span unchanged.
- Changing the doc text ("Doc." to "Docs.") changes the hash.
- Changing the attribute (`inline` to `cold`) changes the hash.
- A leading-blank-line shift leaves the hash unchanged and moves the line numbers.
- Editing a nested item's body changes the parent's structural hash but not its identity hash.
- In `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`), the Rust case changes a block comment and reflows doc prose without changing the hash. Joining the doc words does change it.

**Python.** Decorators contribute, and ordinary comments don't.
- `python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing` shows that changing a decorator, or removing it, changes the hash. Whitespace changes leave it unchanged.
- The same test shows a method's decorator changes the class's structural hash but not its identity hash.
- The bundled test covers `#` comment exclusion. It also covers docstrings, which the Python rules say participate: reflowing keeps the hash, and changing the words changes it.

**TypeScript, TSX, CSS, Markdown, TOML, YAML.** Comments are excluded from the hash.
- Each language has a case in the bundled test whose comment text changes without changing the hash. The TS and TSX cases use doc comments, which the TS rules explicitly exclude.
- The Markdown block comment is excluded, and an inline HTML comment inside a paragraph does count, as the Markdown rules state.
- In every case, joining words does change the hash. Each saved hash is also checked to be 64 hex characters.

**Implementation.** The implementation, `Builder::encode` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/mod.rs`, is reached by these tests. Only the Rust and Python languages produce `Annotation` attachments.

**Gaps.** I found no required distinction the tests would miss. Two things are not tested directly:
- Rust inner versus outer doc grouping. I treated this as part of `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`, not this requirement.
- A plain `//` comment in TypeScript. The harder case, a doc comment, is covered.

I judged both as outside this requirement's obligations.

text: :::{req} attachments.fingerprint
Each language's fingerprint rules determine which attachments
contribute to the owning item's structural hash.
:::{definition} attachment
:phrase: attachment
An *attachment* is a source construct that an outline language associates
with an outline item. A documentation comment on a Rust function and a
decorator on a Python method are examples.
:::{req} attachments
The outline language assigns each {term}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachment`
to one owning item, which may be the file root. Each item lists the
attachments it owns.
:::{req} attachments.comments
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
:::{req} attachments.empty
An item with no attachments has an empty list. A language may return empty
lists for every item.
:::{req} attachments.fingerprint
Each language's fingerprint rules determine which attachments
contribute to the owning item's structural hash.
:::{req} attachments.order
Each item's attachments appear in source order.
:::{req} attachments.span
Each attachment's `span` is a half-open byte range in the original file
snapshot, even when the caller has selected a nested item. Slicing that
snapshot at the span yields the complete source construct, including its
delimiters. Repeated occurrences have their own spans.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} fingerprints
Each line's structural and identity hashes are the SHA-256 digest of its
whitespace-separated words, using the unambiguous encoding under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Whitespace within a line does
not affect its hash; word boundaries remain significant.
The root hash encodes the nonblank lines in source order, including their line
boundaries. Inserting blank lines preserves it. Reordering distinct nonblank
lines or joining them changes the root's structural encoding.
The scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural
hashes. The remaining source structure and text participate in hashing.
:::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
